candidates.summary: the before/after cap counts realms the PR added, which can never carry a before half, so they spend the two slots the modified realms needed
candidates.failure_scenario: a PR adds gno.land/r/a/added and gno.land/r/b/added and edits gno.land/r/z/modified. plan.go:229 builds ChangedRealms with sortedKeys, so the two additions come first. ScreenshotPairs appends a pair for each (Before empty, New true), hits len(pairs) >= maxPairs on the third, breaks, and the only realm with a merge-base rendering gets no comparison at all. The comment shows two single images captioned "New in this PR - nothing to compare against" and the realm the reviewer needs to diff is one link in the list below.
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestScreenshotPairsCapSpentOnAddedRealms -v . in misc/gnopreview with the repro file: expect the modified realm among the pairs, observe both slots taken by the added realms with Before empty
candidates.evidence: pair realm="gno.land/r/a/added" before="" after="_shots/r-a-added-3b55b24d-after.png" new=true / pair realm="gno.land/r/b/added" before="" after="_shots/r-b-added-84738813-after.png" new=true / "i before/after capped at 2 realm(s); the rest are listed as links" — gno.land/r/z/modified, the only realm with a _before/ page, never appears. PASS at ecf7af0f2, go1.25.9.

candidates.summary: an explicit -chrome that does not resolve is silently discarded and auto-detection runs instead
candidates.failure_scenario: findChrome puts the -chrome value at the head of the same candidate slice as google-chrome, chromium and the macOS bundle path, then returns the first entry that LookPath or Stat resolves. A -chrome pointing at a moved or misspelled binary falls through to whatever browser is on PATH, so the operator's one knob for picking the browser does nothing and the screenshots come from a different build than the one they named; where nothing else resolves the message reads "no Chrome/Chromium found" and never mentions that the flag was bad.
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestFindChrome -v . in misc/gnopreview with the repro file: a decoy chromium on PATH and findChrome("/nonexistent/path/to/chrome"); expect "" or an error, observe the decoy

candidates.summary: nothing bounds the Chrome process's wall clock, and the render job declares no timeout-minutes
candidates.failure_scenario: chromeShot calls exec.Command(...).CombinedOutput() with no context and no deadline. --virtual-time-budget=4000 bounds the page's virtual clock, not the process: a Chrome that wedges on startup (profile lock, a crashed zygote, a stuck GPU probe) never returns, ScreenshotPairs never finishes, and since .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml sets no timeout-minutes the render job holds an ubuntu-latest runner to the 6-hour default before GitHub kills it. No other exec in misc/gnopreview uses CommandContext either, but gnodev at main.go:186 is at least reaped by a stop() on defer.
candidates.evidence: both greps return 0 at ecf7af0f2; grep -rn CommandContext misc/gnopreview/ returns nothing.

candidates.summary: the progress line prints "(before/after)" for every appended pair, including the ones that have no before half
candidates.failure_scenario: the Printf sits after the append with no reference to pair.Before, so a realm whose before shot was never attempted (base nil, or base.FileOf miss) or failed still logs "  📷 gno.land/r/a/added (before/after)". Reading the job log, the maintainer sees before/after was produced for every capped realm and only the comment shows otherwise.
candidates.verify_by: the TestScreenshotPairsCapSpentOnAddedRealms output above, where both logged pairs have Before empty
candidates.evidence: "  📷 gno.land/r/a/added (before/after)" printed for a pair whose returned Before is "".

candidates.summary: --no-sandbox is passed unconditionally, including on a maintainer's own machine
candidates.failure_scenario: README.md:54 documents running gnopreview render locally against a contributor's branch. The pages Chrome then loads are HTML the PR's own realms rendered, and the renderer runs with the sandbox off, so a Chrome renderer bug is a full-privilege escape on the maintainer's workstation rather than a contained one. CI needs the flag; a local run does not.
candidates.verify_by: read the exec.Command argument list at shots.go:177-190 and README.md:50-60: the flag is a constant with no CI guard
candidates.evidence: "--no-sandbox" is a literal element of the argument slice, no conditional; README.md:54 shows the local invocation.

candidates.summary: a before shot that failed is indistinguishable in the ShotPair from one that was never attempted, and the comment then shows an unlabelled single image
candidates.failure_scenario: when chromeShot fails for the before half the error goes to stderr and pair.Before stays "" with New false. comment.go:106 renders that case as a bare with no note at all — the note only exists for New — so the reader sees one picture under the realm heading with nothing saying it is the after. The ShotPair doc comment says New exists precisely so the comment does not claim a realm is new when we did not look; the failed-before case falls into the same hole from the other side.
candidates.verify_by: read shots.go:86-96 against comment.go:99-125: the only branch that emits a note tests p.New
candidates.evidence: comment.go:106-113 — note is "" unless p.New, and the img carries alt=p.Realm only.

candidates.summary: the stat error is discarded and every failure reports "chrome wrote no image"
candidates.failure_scenario: os.Stat(out) failing for any reason — a permission error on the _shots directory, a path the umask made unreadable — is reported as "chrome wrote no image", so the job log blames the browser for a filesystem fault and the real errno never reaches the maintainer reading the failed render step.
candidates.verify_by: read shots.go:193-199: err from os.Stat is bound and never used in the returned error
candidates.evidence: if fi, err := os.Stat(out); err != nil || fi.Size() == 0 { return fmt.Errorf("chrome wrote no image") } — err is dropped.

dropped.summary: slug() on the realm URL could traverse out of _shots or collide between two realms
dropped.settled_by: go test -run TestScreenshotPairsCapSpentOnAddedRealms -v . printed "shot written: r-a-added-3b55b24d-after.png": crawl.go:520 maps every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] to '-' so no '/' survives, and appends sha256(s)[:4] whenever the slug differs from its input, which it always does for a path, so two realms cannot share a name.

dropped.summary: the before page is served from outDir but the base crawl writes under _before/, so origin+"/"+beforeFile would 404
dropped.settled_by: crawl.go:142 — p := &page{URL: u, File: path.Join(c.Prefix, urlToFile(u)), Body: body} — and main.go:265 sets Prefix: beforeDir, so base.FileOf already returns "_before/r/.../index.html"; the repro serves exactly that path and chromeShot resolves it.

dropped.summary: Screenshot looks up c.pages[canonicalURL(s.url)] while Run stores c.pages[u] raw, so the three shotPlan entries carrying $ would miss
dropped.settled_by: crawl.go:287-299 — '$' is the webquery separator canonicalURL re-emits (base + "$" + sorted parts), and ':' is the render-args one, so canonicalURL("/r/gnoland/home$source") == "/r/gnoland/home$source", the same key Seeds() queued.

dropped.summary: fi.Size() dereferences a nil FileInfo when os.Stat errors
dropped.settled_by: Go's || short-circuits: err != nil returns before fi.Size() is evaluated. No panic.
